description: The most recent reported value of each metric for one ticker, each with its period (fy, fp), period end, filing date and form. Each metric is its own latest value, so two metrics can come from different periods, and a quarterly fp means ONE quarter's figure, not a year. Pass as_of to use only filings dated on or before that day (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). On a free key, a company outside the full-history sample answers from its most recent reported fiscal year only (history_depth says so) and as_of needs a licence or an evaluation key. Tickers look like AAPL, 2330.TW, 005930.KS, 0403091220.BE, 775670417.FR, CC21860.NZC. Suffixes are not all listed equities, and not all figures mean what the column name suggests. .TW income-statement values are SINGLE-QUARTER (three-month) amounts: Taiwan files cumulative year-to-date totals and they are converted before you see them, so do NOT difference adjacent quarters again. A .TW row with fp FY is the full-year total, not a quarter. .TW current quarters come from the TWSE OpenAPI (Open Government Data License v1.0, attribution required); history from 2013 comes from the TWSE MOPS XBRL archive, which is NOT open data: keep both attribution notices and do not call Taiwan figures open data. US figures (SEC EDGAR) are public information. .TW filing dates are the statutory reporting deadline, a proxy, not the actual release date; for some financial and foreign first-listed companies and for weekend deadlines it can be earlier than the real deadline (known issue, being corrected). .BE is Belgian STATUTORY SOLO accounts, never group consolidation. .NZC is New Zealand REGISTERED CHARITIES (Charities Register annual returns), not listed companies; their `filed` is the register's record date, and about a quarter of those are one day early (known issue, being corrected). .FR is INPI's register of keyed-in annual accounts: `filed` is dateDepot, the register's own deposit date, and balance sheets are included. Coverage is substantially complete from 2022; 2017-2021 is still backfilling. Turnover is lawfully absent from roughly 36% of French deposits (confidentiality declarations); it is PRESENT on 64.0% of company-periods, and the API's /api/v1/fundamentals/quality endpoint reports the measured share of every metric in every market. The reporting model rides in `form` (K consolidated, C complet, S simplifie); consolidated and own accounts are separate deposits with their own dates, so both can appear for one SIREN and period. .DK `filed` is the Copenhagen calendar date of the register's publication, a date only before 11 April 2015. Known issue, being corrected: Danish dates up to 10 April 2015, and some later ones, are one day early, so an as_of query can include a Danish report published the day after as_of (https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology#dk-known-issue). .DK figures are the reporting entity's own accounts: for a Danish-GAAP parent that also publishes group accounts, usually its own figures, not the group's; for an IFRS filer (form annual/ifrs), the consolidated group's. .DK turnover is present on only 10.5% of company-periods (Belgium is lower still at 8.1%) because Danish reporting class B may publish gross profit instead — that absence is lawful disclosure, not missing data, and gross profit is never a substitute for it. A .DK `form` is annual (Danish GAAP) or annual/ifrs, with the period's length appended when a year is not 11-13 months (annual/15m for a long first year); interim reports are excluded. Period labels: fp is FY for an annual row; for a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR year and quarter that contain the period end, not the company's own fiscal quarter: Apple's quarter ending 2025-12-27 is 2025 Q4, which Apple calls Q1 of fiscal 2026, so name a quarter by its period end, not by the label. A latest-view fact with a quarterly fp is ONE quarter's figure, not a full year. Licence: when you relay figures, keep the `attribution` notices and the `licence` notice of the response with them. Known issues, being corrected (also in the known_issues field of each data reply): Some Korean (.KS, .KQ) filing dates are being corrected: where a company first filed a notice extending its annual-report deadline (about 1% of company-years), the year is dated by that notice, so an as_of query can include that year's figures before its report was filed. https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology#kr-known-issue Some Danish (.DK) equity figures, mostly Danish GAAP periods ending 2012 to 2017, may be the company's share capital, not its total equity; for those periods liabilities, debt_to_equity and roe are wrong too. https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology#dk-equity-known-issue

as_of.description: Filing-date cut-off, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2022-01-01). Defaults to today.
